title: impl_defaults parallelization knob names
description: The CANONICAL key names of the parallelization family inside spec.ir.yaml's impl_defaults knob layer (`abstract` and `backend_overrides`), applied by the Compile.static deterministic gate at --stage compile. This exists because the knob layer was un-pinned: four recompiles of one spec produced four different spellings of the same knob (`parallelization` as both a flat string and a mapping; the model knob also as `loop_parallelization` / `loop_parallelism` / `parallelization_model`; the scope knob as `parallel_loop_scope` / `parallel_scope` / `parallelization_scope` / `parallel_loops`; the thread count as `num_threads` / `threads` / `threads_per_rank`; and the whole OpenMP override SECTION as `openmp` or as a `selected.backend_key` such as `cpu_openmp`), and only `backend_overrides.openmp.num_threads` is read by the host renderer — so an aliased thread count, or a correctly-named one under a mis-named section, silently degraded to 1 thread. Consumers of a knob cannot key off a name that changes every regeneration. This schema is a DECLARATIVE COPY: the validator holds the same names as constants and enforces them without file I/O, so an unreadable schema cannot fail-open a running gate. The alias -> canonical table is the load-bearing artifact and lives in the validator, because draft-07 cannot express `this misspelling means that key`. The knob layer stays OPEN (`additionalProperties: true`) — Tune's exploration space is the whole point of a knob, and only the parallelization family is pinned.

abstract.description: Language-independent knobs. Open by design; only the parallelization family below is pinned.

parallelization.description: The parallel execution model as a single FLAT token (`openmp`, `none`, or a novel model such as `openmp+simd` — the vocabulary is deliberately NOT a whitelist, since this is an exploration knob). Two shapes are rejected by the canonical validator: the mapping form (`{method: openmp, apply_to: parallelizable_loops}`), which decomposes into this key plus `parallel_scope` / `parallel_granularity`; and multi-word PROSE such as `OpenMP applied to parallelizable loops`, which is a scope description filed under the model key. `none` is the SANCTIONED way to declare a serial node, and it additionally exempts the node from the `Generate.gate` `!$omp` presence floor (the floor reads that intent generously — `off` / `serial` / `sequential` / `false` / `disabled` and a boolean `false` count too, under the canonical key or any of its aliases — because that direction only ever fails open) — that is the IR-level escape hatch for a node whose only loops are non-parallelizable.

parallel_scope.description: Which loops the parallelization covers — prose naming them (e.g. `the ghost-fill loops of periodic_copy_x and periodic_copy_y`) or a symbolic value such as `parallelizable_loops`. This is the knob the Generate producer reads to decide where directives go.

parallel_granularity.description: Optional. The nesting level parallelism is applied at (e.g. `loop_level`, `interface_loop`).

backend_overrides.description: Per-backend override values. The OpenMP section MUST be keyed by the literal lowercase `openmp` — never by `selected.backend_key` (`cpu_openmp`, `cpu_openmp_x86_64`) — because `tools/runner_renderer.py` looks up that exact key and reads nothing else, so overrides filed under any other section name are silently dropped. Three live IRs file their OpenMP overrides under `cpu_openmp`; two of them request 4 threads and run on 1. Sections for other backends are unconstrained.

num_threads.description: Thread count. CANONICAL — `tools/runner_renderer.py` reads exactly this key, so `threads` / `threads_per_rank` are silently ignored and the run degrades to 1 thread.

chunk_size.description: Schedule chunk size; 0 means the implementation default.

collapse.description: Number of nested loops to collapse into one iteration space.

x-forbidden-examples-note: draft-07 rejects only the TYPE violations on the pinned keys (a string `num_threads`, a mapping `parallelization`). Every alias below is rejected by the canonical validator alone, since a rename remedy cannot be expressed as a schema constraint. Absent sections and novel (non-alias) knob names PASS both, and no key's VALUE vocabulary is whitelisted — the gate is a closed table of misspellings, not an allowlist of knobs or values. Alias DETECTION is case-insensitive, so `Threads` is the same violation as `threads`; a CANONICAL key must additionally be spelled exactly (bare lowercase, no surrounding whitespace), because a consumer looks up the literal key — `NUM_THREADS` and a space-padded `num_threads` are read by nobody and degrade the run to one thread just as an alias does. The `pattern` on `parallelization` and the `minimum` bounds on the integer members are advisory: the canonical validator checks names and TYPES, not ranges, so only the type half of this schema is covered by the agreement test.
x-forbidden-examples: abstract.parallelization: {method: openmp, apply_to: parallelizable_loops}  -> flat token + abstract.parallel_scope
abstract.parallelization: {scheme: openmp, default_schedule: static}  -> flat token + abstract.parallel_scope + backend_overrides.openmp.schedule
abstract.parallelization: OpenMP applied to parallelizable loops  -> the token `openmp`; the prose belongs in abstract.parallel_scope
backend_overrides.cpu_openmp: {num_threads: 4}  -> backend_overrides.openmp (the literal key; a selected.backend_key section is read by nobody)
backend_overrides.openmp.num_threads: "8"  -> an integer, not a string
